chain.label: IMC with low overcast and fog obscuring terrain
chain.trigger: Instrument meteorological conditions (IMC) prevailed at the time of the accident; overcast ceiling at 600 feet

chain.label: Bull Mountain rising to 2,400 ft near the extended runway centerline
chain.trigger: crashed into mountainous terrain in Stuart, Virginia... at an elevation of about 2,400 feet and near the extended centerline of the runway

chain.label: GPS mounted below seat cushion out of view, with expired, non-IFR-certified database
chain.trigger: the GPS was installed between the cockpit seats below the level of the seat cushion... pilots in both seats were required to turn their heads 90 degrees; The GPS database was not current and therefore was not certified for IFR navigation

chain.label: EGPWS installation deferred; airplane returned to line without terrain warning system
chain.trigger: The airplane was not equipped with an enhanced ground proximity warning system (EGPWS)... the accident airplane was 'put back out on the line' and was scheduled for a GPS upgrade and an EGPWS installation at the end of the 2004 racing season

chain.label: GPS autosequenced from BALES LOM to the MTV airport waypoint at the first LOM crossing
chain.trigger: For approaches that required crossing the LOM twice... the GPS would autosequence to the airport at the initial LOM crossing

caused_by.evidence: The airplane was equipped with an IFR-capable GPS receiver, but the database was not current, and the GPS was not certified for IFR navigation

chain.label: Crew failed to notice the autosequence and read MTV distance as distance to BALES
chain.trigger: the pilots using the GPS data to navigate to the BALES LOM and then failing to notice that the GPS had autosequenced to MTV after the airplane passed BALES

caused_by.evidence: the pilots might have mistakenly believed that the airplane was showing distance data to the BALES LOM when, in fact, the airplane was showing distance data to MTV
pilots in both seats were required to turn their heads 90 degrees toward the center of the airplane and then downward to view the screen

chain.label: Approach descent profile flown about 5 nm displaced, keyed to the airport instead of BALES
chain.trigger: the airplane flew an approach that was displaced by about 5 nm compared with the published approach... the descents to 2,600 and 1,400 feet appeared to be keyed to the MAP or MTV rather than to the BALES LOM

caused_by.evidence: the accident approach profile is consistent with the pilots using the GPS data to navigate to the BALES LOM and then failing to notice that the GPS had autosequenced to MTV
Witnesses at MTV said that they heard the airplane pass overhead but did not see it because of the cloud cover

chain.label: Airplane level at 1,400-1,500 ft, only 60-70 ft agl, several miles beyond the airport
chain.trigger: The airplane leveled at 1,400 feet, about 4 nm beyond MTV and 5 nm beyond the MAP... the airplane was flying 'flat and level' about 60 to 70 feet above ground level

caused_by.evidence: after passing the MAP, the airplane continued to descend from 2,600 feet on a course of 305 degrees and leveled off at 1,400 feet, which was again consistent with a 5-nm displacement

chain.label: Missed approach not initiated until 7 to 8 nm beyond the missed approach point
chain.trigger: Radar data indicated that the flight crew initiated the missed approach 7.5 nm beyond the MAP

caused_by.evidence: the missed approach was initiated 7 to 8 nm past the MAP and was not properly executed
The airplane maintained level flight between 1,400 and 1,500 feet for the next 1 minute 13 seconds

chain.label: Straight-ahead climb on runway heading instead of the published climbing right turn
chain.trigger: the accident airplane did not make a climbing right turn, as required in the published missed approach procedure. Instead... the airplane initiated a straight-ahead climb

caused_by.evidence: The airplane then entered a straight-ahead climb on the runway heading

chain.label: Flightpath converged with rising terrain of Bull Mountain with no warning to the crew
chain.trigger: Interpolation of nominal climb rates and a standard turn rate depicted a flightpath that would have kept the airplane clear of terrain

caused_by.evidence: the flightpath that the airplane would have flown if it had entered a climbing right turn... depicted a flightpath that was clear of terrain
the airplane climbed about 700 feet over the next 2 nm before the flight crew declared a missed approach
The accident occurred on Bull Mountain in Stuart, Virginia, at an elevation of about 2,400 feet
The airplane was not equipped with an EGPWS
Bull Mountain was completely obscured by clouds and fog... the visibility was between 0 and 0.25 mile

chain.label: Controlled flight into trees and terrain on the southeast face of Bull Mountain
chain.trigger: The initial impact point was in trees... The airplane came to rest on the southeast face of Bull Mountain at an elevation of about 2,450 feet

caused_by.evidence: crashed into mountainous terrain in Stuart, Virginia, during a missed approach to Martinsville/Blue Ridge Airport

chain.label: Ten occupants killed by blunt force trauma; airplane destroyed
chain.trigger: The two flight crewmembers and eight passengers were killed, and the airplane was destroyed by impact forces and postcrash fire

caused_by.evidence: The Chief Medical Examiner determined that the cause of death for the airplane occupants was blunt force trauma
